steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our ArtAdapter paper on text-to-image style transfer. Cover the challenge and the shortcomings of existing style transfer and diffusion methods, describe our framework and its components, and finish with a list of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. T2I style transfer and its core challenge
2. Limits of existing methods (AST, diffusion-based finetuning)
3. ArtAdapter: multi-level style encoder and Explicit Adaptation
4. Auxiliary Content Adapter, fast finetuning, style mixing
5. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. T2I style transfer
- bridges AI and artistic creativity; text descriptions -> visually rich, stylistic images
- challenge: not just text-resonant images but artistic depth and nuance, delicate brushstrokes to bold composition

2. Existing methods
- conventional arbitrary style transfer (AST): stuck at low-level features (medium, colors)
- diffusion approaches: Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, LoRA -> potential for style representation
- but laborious finetuning, overfitting -> outputs dominated by style reference content, text context lost
- artworks: hard to transfer style from a single reference

3. ArtAdapter
- style embeddings from multi-level style encoder (layers of artistic attributes)
- embeddings interplay with text context in text encoder
- Explicit Adaptation in cross-attention layers: trains style pathway only, text pathway frozen
- textures to distinctive expression represented faithfully, textual generalizability kept

4. Other components
- Auxiliary Content Adapter (ACA), training only: weak content guidance, separates content structure from style references
- fast finetuning: single- and multi-image references, minimal steps, less time/compute, addresses overfitting
- style mixing: multi-level encoder blends styles from several references at different levels

5. Contributions
- (i) ArtAdapter: multi-level encoder + Explicit Adaptation, balance style/text semantics
- (ii) ACA against content dominance
- (iii) fast finetuning
- (iv) style mixing across hierarchical levels

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Text-to-image (T2I) style transfer brings together artificial intelligence and artistic creativity, and it is a very interesting domain that turns textual descriptions into visually rich and stylistic images. The main challenge is not only to generate images that match the text, but also to give them artistic depth and nuance, from delicate brushstrokes to bold compositional elements, so that the essence of the artistic vision is captured. Conventional arbitrary style transfer (AST) methods usually have trouble going beyond low-level features like medium and colors, and they do not capture the more sophisticated parts of artistic expression. Diffusion approaches, including Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), have shown potential for representing style. But these methods need laborious finetuning and they tend to overfit, so the outputs are too influenced by the content of the style references and the textual context gets lost. With artworks, which are unique, these methods especially have difficulties transferring style from a single reference.

- ArtAdapter: style embeddings from multi-level style encoder, interplay with text in text encoder
- Explicit Adaptation in cross-attention layers: style pathway only, text pathway frozen -> faithful style, textual generalizability kept
- ACA in training: weak content guidance, separates content structure from style references
- fast finetuning: single/multi-image references, minimal steps, less time and compute, against overfitting
- style mixing via multi-level encoder
- contributions (i)-(iv): ArtAdapter, ACA, fast finetuning, style mixing

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Text-to-image (T2I) style transfer brings together artificial intelligence and artistic creativity, and it is a very interesting domain that turns textual descriptions into visually rich and stylistic images. The main challenge is not only to generate images that match the text, but also to give them artistic depth and nuance, from delicate brushstrokes to bold compositional elements, so that the essence of the artistic vision is captured. Conventional arbitrary style transfer (AST) methods usually have trouble going beyond low-level features like medium and colors, and they do not capture the more sophisticated parts of artistic expression. Diffusion approaches, including Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), have shown potential for representing style. But these methods need laborious finetuning and they tend to overfit, so the outputs are too influenced by the content of the style references and the textual context gets lost. With artworks, which are unique, these methods especially have difficulties transferring style from a single reference.

To address these challenges, we present ArtAdapter, a new T2I style transfer framework that uses style embeddings from a multi-level style encoder. These style embeddings represent different layers of artistic attributes, and they interact with the textual context inside the text encoder. The style information is then refined more with a new Explicit Adaptation mechanism, which is placed in the cross-attention layers of the diffusion model. The Explicit Adaptation focuses only on the style pathway and the text pathway stays frozen. Because of this, the artistic elements, from basic textures to the distinctive expression of the artworks, are represented faithfully and precisely in the generated images, and the textual generalizability is not compromised. Our approach also uses an Auxiliary Content Adapter (ACA) during training. The ACA gives weak content guidance, which helps to separate the content structure from the style references. This means the final images are not overwhelmed by the content of the style references, and they keep a clear representation of the style elements and of what the text prompt wants. We also introduce a fast finetuning method, which improves the model's ability to capture nuanced style details. This finetuning works for both single- and multi-image style references, and it gets detailed style representation with minimal steps, so it greatly reduces the time and computational resources that are usually required. It deals with the overfitting problem and makes adaptation faster. Another notable feature of ArtAdapter is that it is good at style mixing. Using the multi-level style encoder, ArtAdapter can blend styles from different references by extracting and combining different stylistic elements at different levels. This makes it possible to produce images that blend many artistic influences, which gives a lot of flexibility and creativity to style transfer.

Our main contributions are the following: (i) A new T2I style transfer model, ArtAdapter, which uses a multi-level style encoder and the Explicit Adaptation mechanism to capture different levels of style representation, and keeps a balance between style and textual semantics; (ii) The Auxiliary Content Adapter (ACA), which separates content structure from style references and addresses the problem of content dominance from style references. (iii) A fast finetuning approach for rapid and effective style adaptation; (iv) ArtAdapter allows style mixing across different hierarchical levels, which adds to the creative potential of T2I style transfer.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Bridging artificial intelligence and artistic creativity, text-to-image (T2I) style transfer [1,2,3] is a captivating domain that transforms textual descriptions into visually rich and stylistic representations. The core challenge lies not just in generating text-resonant images but in infusing them with artistic depth and nuance, from delicate brushstrokes to bold compositional elements, thereby capturing the essence of artistic vision. Conventional arbitrary style transfer (AST) methods [4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11] typically struggle beyond low-level features such as medium and colors, failing to grasp the more sophisticated aspects of artistic expression. Diffusion approaches [3,12], including Textual Inversion [13], DreamBooth [14], and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) [15,16], have shown potential in style representation. Yet these methods are hindered by laborious finetuning processes and a tendency to overfit, leading to outputs overly influenced by the content of the style references at the expense of the textual context. Especially given the unique nature of artworks, these methods have difficulty transferring style from a single reference.

To address these challenges, we present ArtAdapter, a novel T2I style transfer framework that uses style embeddings derived from a multi-level style encoder. These style embeddings, representing various layers of artistic attributes, interact with the textual context within the text encoder. The style information is further refined through the novel Explicit Adaptation mechanism, located in the cross-attention layers of the diffusion model. The Explicit Adaptation focuses explicitly on the style pathway while leaving the text pathway frozen. This ensures that artistic elements, from foundational textures to the distinctive expression of the artworks, are faithfully and precisely represented in the generated images without compromising textual generalizability. Moreover, our approach incorporates the Auxiliary Content Adapter (ACA) during training. The ACA offers weak content guidance, helping to separate content structure from the style references. This ensures that the final images are not overwhelmed by the content of the style references, maintaining a clear representation of style elements and of the narrative intent of the text prompts. Furthermore, we introduce a fast finetuning method that further refines the model's ability to capture nuanced style details. This finetuning is effective for both single- and multi-image style references, achieving detailed style representation with minimal steps and greatly reducing the time and computational resources typically required. It addresses the challenge of overfitting and speeds up adaptation. A notable feature of ArtAdapter is its skill at style mixing. Using the multi-level style encoder, ArtAdapter can blend styles from various references, extracting and combining distinct stylistic elements at different levels. This enables images that blend a diverse array of artistic influences, offering great flexibility and creativity in style transfer.

The principal contributions of our work are as follows: (i) A novel T2I style transfer model, ArtAdapter, that uses a multi-level style encoder and the Explicit Adaptation mechanism to capture diverse levels of style representation while balancing style and textual semantics; (ii) The Auxiliary Content Adapter (ACA), which separates content structure from style references, addressing content dominance from style references; (iii) A fast finetuning approach that enables rapid and effective style adaptation; (iv) ArtAdapter supports style mixing across different hierarchical levels, enriching the creative potential of T2I style transfer.
